text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate from inference-api-prod in eu-west-1. Rate spiked to 14% for 5m. Links: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2112 and alert rule #inference-5xx-prod

maria: I'm primary on shift, looking now. pulling logs and checking recent deploys.

devon: I'm secondary, standing by. if it looks like deploy regress, tell me and I can open a rollback.

ashok: quick runbook pointer: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/inference-5xx -> follow the "rate spike" section. Start with checking Nginx LB 5xx vs application 5xx.

maria: rolling tail of logs, see repeated "kv-cache OOM" in model-worker-02 and 03:
```
2026-02-19T08:23:07Z model-worker-02 ERROR kv_cache.cc:142 OOM trying to allocate 512MB
2026-02-19T08:23:08Z inference-api ERR request_id=abc123 status=500 backend=worker-02
```

jen: customer-impact check — SLO alert was paging. Which customers are seeing user-facing errors?

maria: preliminary: 12 customers reported retries in the last 10m, mostly smaller PLG apps in eu-west. No enterprise SLAs yet. Traffic drop on worker-02 correlates with 5xx.

leo: any recent model/quant change pushed? I deployed a quant-profile tweak at 07:58 but it was to canary pool, not prod.

maria: I see a new hotspot: autoscaler moved traffic onto worker-02 after it restarted, then OOMs started. Suspect mem leak or stale artifact.

oncall-manager: Given alert storm risk during handoff and spurious duplicates, propose a temporary threshold bump: change inference-5xx-prod alert from 10%->20% for 30m while we mitigate. Log the change and schedule automatic revert. Anyone object? @devon @ashok

devon: +1 from me, makes sense to avoid paging churn while you triage. Make sure we set a hard revert time.

ashok: agree but add note: create a suppression not silence so we still capture metrics for postmortem. Use alertmanager suppression with tags: incident=INC-2112, author=maria.

maria: will do. Command I'm using (Alertmanager API):
```bash
curl -X POST https://alertmanager.redwood.internal/api/v1/suppression -d '{"rule": "inference-5xx-prod", "threshold": 0.20, "duration": "30m", "meta": {"incident": "INC-2112", "owner": "maria"}}'
```

incident-suppressor-bot: suppression created for rule inference-5xx-prod by maria, expires in 30m. Suppression ID sup-9876.

maria: suppression applied. Also cordoning worker-02 from autoscaler and draining existing requests. Command:
```bash
kubectl label node worker-02 maintenance=true && kubectl drain worker-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

leo: thanks. I can build a quick rollback of the last artifact if we need to revert. Prefer to drain and reprovision first.

jen: regarding customer comms: since enterprise not impacted, no OOB customer notification. Put note in status page if we hit >20% error for >15m after revert.

maria: draining done. worker-02 reports no new 5xx for last 2m, error rate across cluster down to 3%. Monitoring for 10m before finalizing.

devon: I'll keep watch and bump priority if it resurfaces. Recording action items: 1) suppression sup-9876, 2) node drain, 3) follow-up ticket INC-2112-postmortem.

oncall-manager: make sure to capture the SLO temporary adjustment in the incident log and add rollback timestamp (revert at +30m = 1984569690). Also ping customer success if anything changes.

maria: logged everything in INC-2112 and added the runbook section we used. Setting a reminder to revert suppression at expiry.

incident-bot: update: suppression sup-9876 will auto-revert at 30m or when closed.

maria: monitoring steady; will not roll back code now. Leaving suppression until expiry. If rate climbs again we'll escalate and rollback to previous stable artifact.

devon: :thumbsup: keeping eyes. If you want me to take primary after you sign off in 10m, say so.

maria: thanks — I'll handoff primary to @devon if all looks good at +15m.

leo: one small ops note: add KB link to postmortem template for OOM-related worker issues so we don't reinvent steps next time.

maria: done. closing thread for now — will reopen if suppression expires and errors spike again. Will file postmortem if root cause confirmed. :white_check_mark:
